import { Html, Head, Main, NextScript } from 'next/document';

/**
 * Custom Document component
 * Sets base HTML structure, language, and font preloading
 */
export default function Document() {
  return (
    <Html lang="en" className="h-full">
      <Head>
        {/* Inter font from Google Fonts */}
        <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
        <link
          rel="preconnect"
          href="https://fonts.gstatic.com"
          crossOrigin="anonymous"
        />
        <link
          href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600;700&display=swap"
          rel="stylesheet"
        />
        <meta name="application-name" content="FibreFlow Accounting" />
      </Head>
      <body className="h-full antialiased">
        <Main />
        <NextScript />
      </body>
    </Html>
  );
}

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy Accounting App to Velocity Server
set -e

DEPLOY_DIR="/home/velo/accounting"
REPO_DIR="/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting"

echo "=== Deploying Accounting App ==="

# 1. Sync files to deploy directory
echo "Syncing files..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "
  mkdir -p $DEPLOY_DIR
  rsync -a --delete \
    --exclude=node_modules \
    --exclude=.next \
    --exclude=.git \
    --exclude=.env.local \
    $REPO_DIR/ $DEPLOY_DIR/
"

# 2. Copy env file if not exists
if [ ! -f "$DEPLOY_DIR/.env.local" ]; then
  echo "Creating .env.local..."
  sudo -u velo bash -c "cp $REPO_DIR/.env.local $DEPLOY_DIR/.env.local"
fi

# 3. Install deps and build
echo "Installing dependencies..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "cd $DEPLOY_DIR && npm install --production"

echo "Building..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "cd $DEPLOY_DIR && npm run build"

# 4. Install systemd service if not exists
if [ ! -f /etc/systemd/system/fibreflow-accounting.service ]; then
  echo "Installing systemd service..."
  sudo cp $REPO_DIR/scripts/fibreflow-accounting.service /etc/systemd/system/
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo systemctl enable fibreflow-accounting
fi

# 5. Restart service
echo "Restarting service..."
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-accounting

# 6. Check status
sleep 2
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-accounting --no-pager | head -15

echo ""
echo "=== Deploy complete ==="
echo "URL: https://fin.fibreflow.app"

#!/bin/bash
# Accounting App - Database Setup
# Runs all migrations in order against the Neon database

set -e

# Load .env.local if it exists
if [ -f .env.local ]; then
  export $(grep -v '^#' .env.local | xargs)
fi

if [ -z "$DATABASE_URL" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: DATABASE_URL is not set"
  exit 1
fi

echo "=== Accounting Database Setup ==="
echo ""

MIGRATIONS_DIR="scripts/migrations/sql"

# Run migrations in order
for migration in \
  000_users_and_auth.sql \
  200_accounting_foundation.sql \
  201_accounts_payable.sql \
  202_accounts_receivable.sql \
  203_bank_reconciliation.sql \
  204_financial_reporting.sql \
  205_sage_migration.sql \
  210_vat201_data_model.sql; do

  if [ -f "$MIGRATIONS_DIR/$migration" ]; then
    echo "Running: $migration"
    psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f "$MIGRATIONS_DIR/$migration" 2>&1 | tail -5
    echo "  ✓ Done"
    echo ""
  else
    echo "  ⚠ Skipping $migration (not found)"
  fi
done

echo "=== All migrations complete ==="
echo ""

# Seed admin user
echo "Seeding admin user..."
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "
INSERT INTO users (id, email, password_hash, first_name, last_name, role, permissions, is_active)
VALUES (
  'admin-001',
  'admin@accounting.local',
  -- bcrypt hash of 'admin123' (change in production!)
  '\$2b\$12\$uabVX3TLtKt5yMdFm3GioObqpAk43vXvClYnjc9nEm8ISKRMD1jSG',
  'Admin',
  'User',
  'super_admin',
  '[\"*\"]'::JSONB,
  true
)
ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;
"
echo "  ✓ Admin user seeded"

echo ""
echo "=== Setup complete ==="

# Accounting Module

## Purpose
Full double-entry accounting system for FibreFlow. Handles chart of accounts, journal entries, AP/AR, bank reconciliation, financial reporting, and Sage migration.

## Key Services
| Service | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `chartOfAccountsService.ts` | GL account CRUD, account hierarchy |
| `journalEntryService.ts` | Double-entry journal entries |
| `supplierInvoiceService.ts` | AP invoice management, 3-way match |
| `supplierPaymentService.ts` | Supplier payment processing |
| `customerPaymentService.ts` | AR payment allocation |
| `creditNoteService.ts` | Credit note creation/application |
| `bankReconciliationService.ts` | Bank statement import, matching |
| `apAgingService.ts` | Accounts payable aging report |
| `arAgingService.ts` | Accounts receivable aging report |
| `financialReportingService.ts` | Trial balance, income statement, balance sheet |
| `fiscalPeriodService.ts` | Fiscal period open/close management |
| `glIntegrationHooks.ts` | Auto-create GL entries from procurement (GRN, PO) |
| `sageImportService.ts` | Import from Sage accounting |
| `sageMigrationService.ts` | Full Sage migration workflow |

## Utilities
| Utility | Purpose |
|---------|---------|

14 reports across 4 categories: Financial Statements (IS, BS, Cash Flow, Trial Balance), Tax & Budget (VAT Return, Budget vs Actual), Transaction Reports (Customer, Supplier, Bank, Account Transactions, AR Aging, AP Aging), Analysis (Project Profitability, Audit Trail).

### Report Features (Phase 2-4, Feb 2025)
- **Drill-down**: Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Trial Balance, Budget vs Actual — click any account to expand inline transaction detail
- **Cost centre filtering**: Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Trial Balance — dropdown loads from `/api/accounting/cost-centres`
- **Comparative periods**: Income Statement (prior period), Balance Sheet (prior year), Trial Balance (compare period) — shows Prior/Current/Variance columns
- **CSV export**: All 13 report pages have Export CSV buttons → dedicated `*-export.ts` API routes

## Critical Rules
- All journal entries MUST balance (total debits = total credits)
- GL integration hooks auto-fire on GRN confirm and PO approval
- Fiscal periods must be open before posting entries
- Bank reconciliation uses auto-match before manual matching
- 3-way match: PO amount vs GRN quantity vs Invoice amount
- **gl_journal_lines uses `gl_account_id` NOT `account_id`** — always JOIN with `jl.gl_account_id = ga.id`
- `account_subtype` column exists on `gl_accounts` but may be NULL — use `hasSubtype` detection pattern with fallback to `account_name ILIKE` matching
- Neon returns numeric values as strings — always `Number()` before arithmetic
- **Neon returns Date objects for DATE columns** — `String(dateObj).split('T')[0]` fails; use `dateObj instanceof Date ? dateObj.toISOString().split('T')[0] : String(val).split('T')[0]`
- **gl_journal_entries has NO `total_debit`/`total_credit` columns** — must compute via `SUM(jl.debit)` / `SUM(jl.credit)` JOIN on `gl_journal_lines`
- **users table** has `first_name` + `last_name` (NOT `name`) and `id` is `VARCHAR(255)` (NOT UUID) — cast both sides for JOINs: `u.id::TEXT = je.created_by::TEXT`
- **No conditional SQL fragments** — `${cond ? sql\`AND x\` : sql\`\`}` breaks Neon; use nullable param pattern: `(${ccId}::TEXT IS NULL OR jl.cost_center_id = ${ccId}::UUID)`

- No routing conflicts with the Next.js app

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy Accounting App to Velocity Server
set -e

DEPLOY_DIR="/home/velo/accounting"
REPO_DIR="/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting"

echo "=== Deploying Accounting App ==="

# 1. Sync files to deploy directory
echo "Syncing files..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "
  mkdir -p $DEPLOY_DIR
  rsync -a --delete \
    --exclude=node_modules \
    --exclude=.next \
    --exclude=.git \
    --exclude=.env.local \
    $REPO_DIR/ $DEPLOY_DIR/
"

# 2. Copy env file if not exists
if [ ! -f "$DEPLOY_DIR/.env.local" ]; then
  echo "Creating .env.local..."
  sudo -u velo bash -c "cp $REPO_DIR/.env.local $DEPLOY_DIR/.env.local"
fi

# 3. Install deps and build
echo "Installing dependencies..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "cd $DEPLOY_DIR && npm install --production"

echo "Building..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "cd $DEPLOY_DIR && npm run build"

# 4. Install systemd service if not exists
if [ ! -f /etc/systemd/system/fibreflow-accounting.service ]; then
  echo "Installing systemd service..."
  sudo cp $REPO_DIR/scripts/fibreflow-accounting.service /etc/systemd/system/
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo systemctl enable fibreflow-accounting
fi

# 5. Restart service
echo "Restarting service..."
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-accounting

# 6. Check status
sleep 2
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-accounting --no-pager | head -15

echo ""
echo "=== Deploy complete ==="
echo "URL: https://fin.fibreflow.app"

[Unit]
Description=Accounting App (Next.js)
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=velo
Group=velo
WorkingDirectory=/home/velo/accounting
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /home/velo/accounting/node_modules/.bin/next start -p 3101
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5
Environment=NODE_ENV=production
Environment=PORT=3101
EnvironmentFile=/home/velo/accounting/.env.local

# Logging
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal
SyslogIdentifier=accounting

# Security
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ReadWritePaths=/home/velo/accounting

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

payload.prompt: what do you think is the best colour scheme for isaflow?

payload.last_assistant_message:
For a financial/accounting app like IsaFlow, I'd recommend **teal** over the current emerald. Here's my thinking:

**Why teal works better:**
- Blends blue (trust, stability) + green (finance, money) — best of both
- Differentiates from Sage (green), Xero (blue), QuickBooks (green)
- Feels modern and premium without being flashy
- Works beautifully on dark backgrounds — better contrast than pure emerald

**Suggested palette:**

| Element | Current | Proposed |
|---------|---------|----------|
| Primary accent | `emerald-500` (#10b981) | `teal-500` (#14b8a6) |
| Active nav | `emerald-400` | `teal-400` (#2dd4bf) |
| Buttons | `emerald-600` | `teal-600` (#0d9488) |
| Hover | `emerald-700` | `teal-700` (#0f766e) |
| Sidebar logo | `emerald-600` bg | `teal-600` bg |
| Focus rings | `emerald` | `teal` |

The change would be minimal code-wise — the `ModuleNav` already uses an `accentColor` prop, and most accent references are just `emerald-*` classes.

Alternatively, **indigo** (`#6366f1`) would give a more premium/fintech feel — think Stripe, Plaid — but it's a bigger departure.

Want me to swap the color scheme to teal (or another option)?

Here's what would set IsaFlow apart from Sage/Xero/QuickBooks in the SA market, prioritized by impact:

### High Impact — Competitive Differentiators

**1. AI Bank Categorization**
- Auto-categorize imported bank transactions using pattern matching + LLM
- Learn from user corrections over time
- You already have bank rules — this supercharges them

**2. SARS eFiling Integration**
- Auto-generate VAT201 from your existing VAT data
- Submit directly to SARS via their API
- Tax season compliance reminders
- *This alone would sell the product in SA*

**3. Live Bank Feeds**
- Integrate with Stitch, Plaid or SA open banking APIs (Investec, FNB, Standard Bank)
- Auto-import transactions daily instead of manual CSV upload
- Real-time cash position

**4. Invoice PDF + Email**
- Generate branded PDF invoices with company logo
- Email directly to customers from IsaFlow
- Track if opened/paid
- Payment link integration (Yoco, PayFast, Peach Payments)

### Medium Impact — Power User Features

**5. Multi-Entity / Multi-Company**
- Single login, switch between companies
- Consolidated reporting across entities
- *Critical for accountants managing multiple clients*

**6. Cash Flow Forecasting**
- AI-projected cash flow based on historical patterns
- Factor in recurring invoices, known expenses, seasonal trends
- "You'll run out of cash in 42 days" alerts

**7. Document OCR / Receipt Capture**
- Snap a photo of a receipt or supplier invoice
- Auto-extract date, amount, vendor, VAT
- Match to existing transactions
- Could use Claude vision API for this

**8. Dashboard KPIs**
- Gross profit margin trend
- Debtor days / Creditor days
- Burn rate
- Revenue MoM growth
- Customizable widget grid

### Nice to Have — Polish

**9. Approval Workflows**
- Configurable: invoices over R10k need manager approval
- Email/push notifications
- Audit trail of who approved what

**10. PWA Mobile App**
- The app is already responsive — add a service worker + manifest
- Quick invoice creation on the go
- Push notifications for overdue invoices

**11. Client Portal**
- Customers self-serve: view invoices, download statements, make payments
- Reduces admin overhead

**12. Payroll Integration**
- Connect to PaySpace/SimplePay via API
- Auto-create GL journals from payroll runs

---

**My recommendation for the first sprint:** Items **1, 4, and 8** — AI bank categorization, invoice PDFs with email, and a KPI dashboard. These are high-visibility features that require no external API agreements and build on what you already have.

Want me to start on any of these?

payload.last_assistant_message:
Build your own. Here's why:

**SA payroll is formulaic, not complex:**
- PAYE tax tables — SARS publishes fixed brackets annually
- UIF — flat 1% employee + 1% employer, capped
- SDL — 1% of total payroll
- Medical aid tax credits — fixed monthly amounts per dependant
- Retirement fund deductions — percentage-based

**The entire calculation engine is ~500 lines of TypeScript.** The tax tables are public data, not proprietary. You don't need PaySpace or SimplePay for this.

**What to build:**

| Module | What it does |
|--------|-------------|
| **Employee Register** | Personal details, tax number, bank details, contract type |
| **Pay Structure** | Basic salary, allowances (travel, housing, cell), deductions |
| **Payroll Run** | Monthly calc: gross → PAYE → UIF → SDL → net pay |
| **Payslips** | PDF generation per employee |
| **IRP5/IT3(a)** | Year-end tax certificates |
| **EMP201** | Monthly SARS submission (PAYE + UIF + SDL) |
| **EMP501** | Bi-annual reconciliation |
| **GL Integration** | Auto-journal: salaries expense, PAYE liability, UIF liability, bank |

**Advantages of building it in-house:**
- GL journals post automatically — no CSV import/mapping
- Single source of truth for employee costs in reports
- No per-employee licensing fees (SimplePay charges R25/employee/month)
- Full control over IRP5 generation
- Differentiator — very few SA cloud accounting apps include payroll natively

**The SARS tax tables change once a year** (budget speech in February). One annual update to a config file.

Want me to include this as a full module in the feature plan?

# Research Skill

## 🎯 Load Full PAI Context

**Before starting any task with this skill, load complete PAI context:**

`read ~/.claude/.claude/skills/CORE/SKILL.md`

This provides access to:
- Complete contact list and team members

## When to Use This Skill

This skill activates when the user requests research or information gathering:
- "Do research on X"
- "Research this topic"
- "Find information about X"
- "Investigate this subject"
- "Analyze trends in X"
- "Current events research"
- Any comprehensive information gathering request

**THREE RESEARCH MODES:**

**QUICK RESEARCH MODE:**
- User says "quick research" → Launch 3 agents (1 of each type)
- **Timeout: 2 minutes** | Main Kai waits 2 minutes then synthesizes
- Best for: Simple queries, straightforward questions

**STANDARD RESEARCH MODE (Default):**
- Default for most research requests → Launch 9 agents (3 of each type)
- **Timeout: 3 minutes** | Main Kai waits 3 minutes then synthesizes
- Best for: Most research needs, comprehensive coverage

**EXTENSIVE RESEARCH MODE:**
- User says "extensive research" → Launch 24 agents (8 of each type)
- Use be-creative skill with UltraThink for maximum query diversity
- Generate 24 unique, creative research angles
- **Timeout: 10 minutes** | Main Kai waits 10 minutes then synthesizes
- Best for: Deep-dive research, multi-domain analysis, comprehensive reports

**⏱️ CRITICAL TIMEOUT RULES:**
- **Quick (3 agents): 2 minute timeout**
- **Standard (9 agents): 3 minute timeout**
- **Extensive (24 agents): 10 minute timeout**
- After timeout, main Kai STOPS WAITING and synthesizes with whatever results are available
- Proceed with partial results - don't wait indefinitely for stragglers

## How to Execute

**Execute the `/conduct-research` slash command**, which handles the complete workflow:

1. Decomposing research questions into 3-24 sub-questions
2. Launching up to 24 parallel research agents (perplexity, claude, gemini)
3. Collecting results in 15-60 seconds (**HARD TIMEOUT: 3 minutes max**)
4. Synthesizing findings with confidence levels (even with partial results)
5. Formatting comprehensive report with source attribution

## Available Research Agents

- **perplexity-researcher**: Fast Perplexity API searches (web/current)
- **claude-researcher**: Claude WebSearch with intelligent query decomposition (academic/detailed)
- **gemini-researcher**: Google Gemini multi-perspective research (synthesis)

## Speed Benefits

- ❌ **Old approach**: Sequential searches → 5-10 minutes
- ✅ **Quick mode**: 3 parallel agents → **2 minute timeout**
- ✅ **Standard mode**: 9 parallel agents → **3 minute timeout**
- ✅ **Extensive mode**: 24 parallel agents → **10 minute timeout**

**⏱️ CRITICAL: After timeout, proceed with whatever results are available. DO NOT wait indefinitely for slow agents.**

## 📁 Scratchpad → History Pattern

**Working Directory (Scratchpad):** `~/.claude/scratchpad/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS_research-[topic]/`

**Process:**

1. **Scratchpad (Working Files - Temporary):**
   - Create timestamped directory for each research project
   - Store raw research outputs from all agents
   - Keep intermediate synthesis notes
   - Save query decomposition and analysis
   - Draft reports and iterations

2. **History (Permanent Archive):**
   - Move to `~/.claude/history/research/YYYY-MM-DD_[topic]/` when complete
   - Include: `README.md`, final research report, key data files
   - Archive for future reference and reuse

3. **Verification (MANDATORY):**
   - Check if hooks captured output to history automatically
   - If hooks failed, manually save to history
   - Confirm all files present in history directory

tool_input.content:
---
name: AutoResearch
description: "Autonomous codebase analysis that spawns parallel agents to examine architecture, code quality, performance, security, DX, and dependencies — then synthesizes findings into a prioritized improvement report. USE WHEN the user says 'autoresearch', 'analyze codebase', 'codebase audit', 'code review everything', 'how can we improve', 'find issues', 'codebase health check', or wants a comprehensive automated review of their project."
---

# AutoResearch Skill

## Purpose

Perform a comprehensive, parallelized audit of a codebase by spawning specialized research agents that each focus on a different quality dimension. Synthesize all findings into a single prioritized improvement report.

## When to Use

- User says "autoresearch", "run autoresearch", "analyze this codebase"
- User asks "how can we improve this project"
- User wants a full codebase health check or audit
- User asks for improvement suggestions across the whole project

## Research Dimensions

Launch **6 parallel agents**, each investigating one dimension:

### 1. Architecture Agent
- Project structure and organization
- Component coupling and cohesion
- Route organization and page structure
- Shared vs duplicated code
- Module boundaries and separation of concerns

### 2. Code Quality Agent
- TypeScript strictness and type coverage
- Error handling patterns (empty catches, unhandled promises)
- Code duplication (DRY violations)
- File sizes (flag files > 300 lines)
- Consistent patterns and conventions
- Dead code and unused exports

### 3. Performance Agent
- Bundle size concerns (large imports, tree-shaking issues)
- Unnecessary re-renders (React-specific)
- Data fetching patterns (waterfalls, missing caching)
- Image optimization
- Lazy loading opportunities
- SSR vs CSR decisions

### 4. Security Agent
- Exposed secrets or credentials in code
- Input validation and sanitization
- Auth/session handling patterns
- CSRF, XSS, injection vectors
- Dependency vulnerabilities (check package.json)
- API route protection

### 5. Developer Experience (DX) Agent
- Build and dev tooling (scripts, config)
- Testing coverage and quality
- Linting and formatting setup
- Documentation gaps
- Onboarding friction
- CI/CD pipeline quality

### 6. Dependencies & Infra Agent
- Outdated or vulnerable dependencies
- Unused dependencies
- Missing essential dependencies
- Deployment configuration
- Environment configuration
- Database/API integration patterns

## Execution Workflow

### Step 1: Context Gathering (Main Agent)
Before spawning researchers, quickly gather:
```
- package.json (deps, scripts)
- tsconfig.json (TS config)
- Project structure (top-level dirs)
- Git log (recent activity)
- Any existing CLAUDE.md or README
```

### Step 2: Spawn 6 Parallel Research Agents
Launch all 6 agents simultaneously using the Agent tool. Each agent:
- Receives the project context from Step 1
- Focuses ONLY on its assigned dimension

# AutoResearch Skill

## Purpose

Perform a comprehensive, parallelized audit of a codebase by spawning specialized research agents that each focus on a different quality dimension. Synthesize all findings into a single prioritized improvement report.

## When to Use

- User says "autoresearch", "run autoresearch", "analyze this codebase"
- User asks "how can we improve this project"
- User wants a full codebase health check or audit
- User asks for improvement suggestions across the whole project

## Research Dimensions

Launch **6 parallel agents**, each investigating one dimension:

### 1. Architecture Agent
- Project structure and organization
- Component coupling and cohesion
- Route organization and page structure
- Shared vs duplicated code
- Module boundaries and separation of concerns

### 2. Code Quality Agent
- TypeScript strictness and type coverage
- Error handling patterns (empty catches, unhandled promises)
- Code duplication (DRY violations)
- File sizes (flag files > 300 lines)
- Consistent patterns and conventions
- Dead code and unused exports

### 3. Performance Agent
- Bundle size concerns (large imports, tree-shaking issues)
- Unnecessary re-renders (React-specific)
- Data fetching patterns (waterfalls, missing caching)
- Image optimization
- Lazy loading opportunities
- SSR vs CSR decisions

### 4. Security Agent
- Exposed secrets or credentials in code
- Input validation and sanitization
- Auth/session handling patterns
- CSRF, XSS, injection vectors
- Dependency vulnerabilities (check package.json)
- API route protection

### 5. Developer Experience (DX) Agent
- Build and dev tooling (scripts, config)
- Testing coverage and quality
- Linting and formatting setup
- Documentation gaps
- Onboarding friction
- CI/CD pipeline quality

### 6. Dependencies & Infra Agent
- Outdated or vulnerable dependencies
- Unused dependencies
- Missing essential dependencies
- Deployment configuration
- Environment configuration
- Database/API integration patterns

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy IsaFlow App to Velocity Server
set -e

DEPLOY_DIR="/home/velo/isaflow"
REPO_DIR="/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting"
SERVICE_NAME="isaflow"

echo "=== Deploying IsaFlow ==="

# 1. Sync files to deploy directory
echo "Syncing files..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "
  mkdir -p $DEPLOY_DIR
  rsync -a --delete \
    --exclude=node_modules \
    --exclude=.next \
    --exclude=.git \
    --exclude=.env.local \
    --exclude=tests \
    --exclude=test-results \
    $REPO_DIR/ $DEPLOY_DIR/
"

# 2. Copy env file if not exists
if [ ! -f "$DEPLOY_DIR/.env.local" ]; then
  echo "Creating .env.local..."
  sudo -u velo bash -c "cp $REPO_DIR/.env.local $DEPLOY_DIR/.env.local"
fi

# 3. Install deps and build
echo "Installing dependencies..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "cd $DEPLOY_DIR && npm install --production"

echo "Building..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "cd $DEPLOY_DIR && npm run build"

# 4. Install systemd service
if [ ! -f /etc/systemd/system/${SERVICE_NAME}.service ]; then
  echo "Installing systemd service..."
  sudo cp $REPO_DIR/scripts/${SERVICE_NAME}.service /etc/systemd/system/
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo systemctl enable $SERVICE_NAME
fi

# 5. Install nginx config if not exists
if [ ! -f /etc/nginx/sites-available/app-isaflow ]; then
  echo "Installing nginx config..."
  sudo cp $REPO_DIR/scripts/nginx-app-isaflow /etc/nginx/sites-available/app-isaflow
  sudo ln -sf /etc/nginx/sites-available/app-isaflow /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/app-isaflow
  sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
fi

# 6. Restart service
echo "Restarting service..."
sudo systemctl restart $SERVICE_NAME

# 7. Check status
sleep 2
sudo systemctl status $SERVICE_NAME --no-pager | head -15

echo ""
echo "=== Deploy complete ==="
echo "App: https://app.isaflow.co.za"

tool_input.prompt:
Build a KPI Dashboard for the IsaFlow accounting app at /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting.

## Codebase Patterns (MUST follow exactly)
- Database: `import { sql } from '@/lib/neon'` — tagged templates
- API routes: `import { apiResponse } from '@/lib/apiResponse'` + `withAuth(withErrorHandler(handler as any))`
- Pages use `AppLayout` from `@/components/layout/AppLayout`
- Charts: `recharts` is already installed (v3.6.0)
- Colors: teal color scheme (bg-teal-500, text-teal-400, border-teal-500)
- Read existing files first to understand patterns

## What to Build

### 1. KPI Service (`src/modules/accounting/services/kpiService.ts`)
Functions that query the database for real-time KPIs:

- `getDashboardKPIs(fromDate: string, toDate: string)` returning:
  - **Revenue & Profit**: total revenue, total expenses, gross profit, gross profit margin %, net profit, net profit margin %
  - **Cash Position**: total cash across all bank accounts, cash change vs prior period
  - **Receivables**: total outstanding AR, average debtor days (based on invoice dates vs payment dates), overdue amount
  - **Payables**: total outstanding AP, average creditor days, overdue amount
  - **Activity**: invoices issued this period, payments received, journal entries posted
  
- `getRevenueChart(months: number)` — monthly revenue + expenses for last N months (for line/bar chart)
- `getCashFlowChart(months: number)` — monthly cash inflows vs outflows
- `getAgingBreakdown(type: 'ar' | 'ap')` — current, 30, 60, 90+ day buckets with amounts
- `getTopCustomers(limit: number)` — top N customers by revenue
- `getTopExpenseCategories(limit: number)` — top N GL accounts by expense amount

The queries should use the existing tables: gl_accounts, journal_entries, journal_entry_lines, customer_invoices, supplier_invoices, bank_accounts, bank_transactions, etc. Look at the existing financial reporting service and aging services for query patterns.

### 2. KPI API Route (`pages/api/accounting/kpi-dashboard.ts`)
- GET `/api/accounting/kpi-dashboard` — returns all KPI data
- Query params: `from`, `to`, `months` (for charts, default 6)

### 3. KPI Dashboard Page — REPLACE the Overview tab content
The main accounting page at `pages/accounting/index.tsx` has an "Overview" tab (the default tab). Currently it shows basic stat cards and quick links. REPLACE the Overview tab content with a proper KPI dashboard.

DO NOT modify the entire file — only replace the `renderOverview()` function content (or equivalent section that renders when activeTab === 'overview').

Read the existing `pages/accounting/index.tsx` first to understand the structure, then surgically replace just the overview content.

The new dashboard should have:

**Row 1 — Key Metrics (4 cards)**
- Revenue (with % change vs prior period, teal for positive, red for negative)
- Gross Profit (with margin %)
- Cash Position (total across bank accounts)  
- Outstanding AR (with overdue amount in red)

**Row 2 — Charts (2 columns)**
- Left: Revenue vs Expenses line chart (recharts `LineChart` with `ResponsiveContainer`, 6 months)
- Right: Cash Flow bar chart (inflows green, outflows red, 6 months)

**Row 3 — Tables (2 columns)**
- Left: Top 5 Customers by Revenue (table with name, revenue, invoice count)
- Right: Top 5 Expense Categories (table with account name, total, % of expenses)

**Row 4 — Aging Donut Charts (2 columns)**
- Left: AR Aging (PieChart donut — current, 30, 60, 90+)
- Right: AP Aging (PieChart donut — current, 30, 60, 90+)

**Row 5 — Quick Actions** (keep existing quick links from the current overview)

Use these recharts components: `LineChart, Line, BarChart, Bar, PieChart, Pie, Cell, XAxis, YAxis, CartesianGrid, Tooltip, Legend, ResponsiveContainer`

Color palette for charts:
- Revenue/positive: teal-500 (#14b8a6)
- Expenses/negative: rose-500 (#f43f5e)  
- Cash in: teal-400 (#2dd4bf)
- Cash out: orange-400 (#fb923c)
- Aging buckets: teal-500, amber-400, orange-500, rose-500

### CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS
- Must work in both dark and light theme
- Charts must have proper dark theme support (text colors, grid lines)
- Responsive layout — stack on mobile
- Use real data from the database, not hardcoded values
- Handle empty state gracefully (show R 0 / "No data" / flat charts, not errors)
- Format currency as South African Rand (R prefix, 2 decimals, comma thousands)
- No stubs, no TODOs — complete implementation

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS employees (
  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  employee_number VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  first_name    VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  last_name     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  id_number     VARCHAR(13),
  tax_number    VARCHAR(20),
  start_date    DATE NOT NULL,
  termination_date DATE,
  bank_name     VARCHAR(100),
  bank_account_number VARCHAR(30),
  bank_branch_code VARCHAR(10),
  department    VARCHAR(100),
  position      VARCHAR(100),
  employment_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'permanent'
    CHECK (employment_type IN ('permanent', 'contract', 'temporary')),
  pay_frequency VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'monthly'
    CHECK (pay_frequency IN ('monthly', 'weekly')),
  status        VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'inactive')),
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_employees_employee_number ON employees (employee_number);

);

Build Invoice PDF Generation and Email Delivery for the IsaFlow accounting app at /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting.

## Codebase Patterns (MUST follow exactly)
- Database: `import { sql } from '@/lib/neon'` — tagged templates
- API routes: `import { apiResponse } from '@/lib/apiResponse'` + `withAuth(withErrorHandler(handler as any))`
- jsPDF is already installed (`jspdf` v4.2.0 + `jspdf-autotable` v5.0.7)
- Existing statement PDF generation exists at `src/modules/accounting/utils/statementPdf.ts` — use as reference for PDF patterns
- Colors: teal (#14b8a6) for branding in PDFs
- Read existing files first to understand patterns

## What to Build

### 1. Invoice PDF Service (`src/modules/accounting/services/invoicePdfService.ts`)

Function `generateInvoicePdf(invoiceId: string): Promise<Buffer>` that:
1. Queries the invoice with all line items, client details, company settings
2. Generates a professional PDF invoice with:
   - **Header**: Company name "IsaFlow" (or from settings), company address, VAT number, contact info
   - **Invoice Details**: Invoice number, date, due date, reference
   - **Client Details**: Company name, address, contact, VAT number
   - **Line Items Table**: Description, quantity, unit price, VAT, line total (use jspdf-autotable)
   - **Totals Section**: Subtotal, VAT (15%), Total Due
   - **Payment Details**: Bank name, account number, branch code, reference
   - **Footer**: Terms & conditions, "Generated by IsaFlow"
3. Use teal (#14b8a6) for header bar and accents
4. Return the PDF as a Buffer

Also create `generateCreditNotePdf(creditNoteId: string)` with similar layout but "CREDIT NOTE" header.

### 2. Email Service (`src/modules/accounting/services/emailService.ts`)

Create a generic email service using nodemailer (add to package.json if not present — use `bun add nodemailer @types/nodemailer`):

```typescript
interface EmailOptions {
  to: string | string[];
  subject: string;
  html: string;
  attachments?: Array<{ filename: string; content: Buffer; contentType: string }>;
}
```

- `sendEmail(options: EmailOptions): Promise<{ success: boolean; messageId?: string }>`
- Use SMTP config from environment variables: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, SMTP_FROM
- If SMTP is not configured, log a warning and return `{ success: false }` gracefully

Create `sendInvoiceEmail(invoiceId: string, recipientEmail: string): Promise<void>` that:
1. Generates the invoice PDF
2. Sends email with:
   - Subject: "Invoice {INV-001} from {CompanyName}"
   - HTML body: Professional template with invoice summary, amount due, due date, and "View Invoice" note
   - Attachment: The invoice PDF

### 3. Invoice Email Tracking
Add to migration (`scripts/migrations/invoice-emails.sql`):
```sql
ALTER TABLE customer_invoices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email_sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
ALTER TABLE customer_invoices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email_sent_to TEXT;
ALTER TABLE customer_invoices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email_message_id TEXT;
```

### 4. API Routes

**`pages/api/accounting/invoice-pdf.ts`**
- GET `?invoiceId=xxx` — returns PDF as download (Content-Type: application/pdf, Content-Disposition: attachment)

**`pages/api/accounting/invoice-email.ts`**
- POST `{ invoiceId, recipientEmail }` — generate PDF + send email + update tracking fields

**`pages/api/accounting/credit-note-pdf.ts`**
- GET `?creditNoteId=xxx` — returns credit note PDF as download

### 5. UI Integration

Update the customer invoice detail page (`pages/accounting/customer-invoices/[invoiceId].tsx`):
- Read it first to understand current structure
- Add two buttons to the action bar:
  1. "Download PDF" — links to `/api/accounting/invoice-pdf?invoiceId={id}` (opens in new tab)
  2. "Email Invoice" — opens a small modal asking for recipient email (pre-filled from client record), sends via API, shows success toast

Also update `pages/accounting/credit-notes/[creditNoteId].tsx`:
- Add "Download PDF" button

### CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS
- PDF must look professional — proper formatting, alignment, colors
- Email HTML template must render well in all email clients (use tables for layout, inline CSS)
- Handle missing SMTP config gracefully (don't crash, just warn)
- Currency formatting: R prefix, 2 decimals, comma thousands separator
- No stubs, no TODOs — complete implementation
- Test the PDF generation works with jsPDF in Node.js context

- **`pages/accounting/customer-invoices/index.tsx:13` — `formatCurrency` duplicated 39 times** — The `formatCurrency(amount)` helper is defined inline in **39 separate page files**, always with identical `en-ZA` / `ZAR` locale settings. Same pattern repeated for `formatDate` (9 files) and `StatusBadge` (14 files). These are prime candidates for shared utility extraction but no such file exists. Fix: create `src/utils/formatters.ts` (currency, date) and `src/components/ui/StatusBadge.tsx` and import them everywhere.

- **`pages/accounting/bank-transactions/index.tsx:98–264` — 9 silent empty catch blocks** — This single file has **9 instances** of `.catch(() => {})`. Silent failures here mean bank transaction load errors, account lookups, and category fetches all fail invisibly. Across the app, 17 total `.catch(() => {})` occurrences exist in pages. Fix: at minimum log with `log.warn()` or propagate the error to the page's existing `setError` state.

- **`src/modules/accounting/services/financialReportingService.ts:18` — `type Row = any`** — All 28 service files use `type Row = any` as a workaround for Neon's untyped SQL result rows. This nullifies TypeScript's protection on every single database result mapping. Fix: define typed row interfaces per query result or use a lightweight `Record<string, unknown>` with assertion helpers.

---

This inconsistency makes route discovery harder and colocation of feature-related files impossible for the flat pages. Fix: migrate flat pages to subdirectory format.

- **`pages/accounting/audit-trail.tsx:1`, `pages/accounting/bank-rules.tsx:1`, `pages/accounting/reports/customer.tsx:1`, `pages/accounting/reports/trial-balance.tsx:1`** — Four pages are pure re-export aliases (`export { default } from './reports/audit-trail'`). These exist to handle legacy or alternative URLs but add noise to the route tree. Fix: use Next.js `redirects` in `next.config.js` instead of ghost page files.

- **`pages/api/accounting/` — Flat API route directory with 120+ files** — All API routes live in one flat directory with inconsistent naming: some are `noun-verb.ts` (`bank-rules-action.ts`, `bank-rules-preview.ts`, `bank-rules-seed.ts`), others are just `noun.ts`, and reports are mixed (`reports-income-statement.ts` vs `reports/sales-by-item.ts`). Fix: adopt a consistent `/api/accounting/[resource]/index.ts` structure and move all `reports-*` files into `reports/` subdirectory to match the convention already started there.

- **`pages/accounting/credit-notes/index.tsx` vs `pages/accounting/customer-credit-notes.tsx` vs `pages/accounting/supplier-credit-notes.tsx`** — Three pages cover the same "credit notes" domain from different angles. Fix: extract a generic `<InvoiceListPage>` or `<CreditNoteListPage>` component parameterised by type (customer/supplier), or use a shared hook `usePaginatedList(endpoint, filters)`.

- **`pages/api/accounting/customer-invoices-list.ts:24–52` — Duplicated SQL branches** — The GET handler runs two nearly identical `sql` template strings that differ only in a `WHERE ci.status = ${status}` clause. Fix: build the query conditionally using the service-layer pattern already used by `supplierInvoiceService.getSupplierInvoices()`.

### Suggestions

- **`src/hooks/` — Empty directory** — There are no custom hooks despite the app having repeated patterns of `useState + useEffect + useCallback + fetch` that appear identically across 40+ pages. The `usePaginatedList`, `useReport`, and `useFormWithSubmit` patterns each appear 15–25 times. Fix: create reusable hooks such as `src/hooks/useFilteredList.ts` that encapsulates the load/error/filter state machine.

- **`src/components/accounting/` — Only 15 components for 100+ pages** — The component library is extremely thin relative to page count. Almost all table headers, filter bars, export buttons, error states, and loading states are inlined per-page instead of extracted. Fix: prioritise a `<PageHeader>`, `<FilterBar>`, `<DataTable>`, and `<ErrorBanner>` component to eliminate the most common duplicated JSX.

- **`src/services/vfStorageAdapter.ts`** — A single file lives in `src/services/` (top level) while all other services live in `src/modules/accounting/services/`. This is an orphaned file outside the module boundary. Fix: move into the module or create an explicit `src/services/` layer with an `index.ts`.

- **`src/types/procurement/` and `src/types/storage.types.ts`** — Two type files live outside the `src/modules/accounting/types/` structure, suggesting an in-progress or leftover migration from the FibreFlow parent app. Fix: consolidate all app types under `src/modules/accounting/types/` or a top-level `src/types/` with a clear naming convention.

- **No custom hooks layer** — There is no `src/hooks/` directory content. The auth polling in `AuthContext`, localStorage hydration in `AppLayout`, and every data-fetching page all re-implement the same async state pattern. Fix: extract `useAsync`, `useLocalStorage`, and a generic `useApiList<T>` hook.

- **`pages/api/accounting/` — No Zod validation on request bodies** — Although Zod is listed as a stack dependency, none of the 10 API routes sampled perform schema validation on `req.body`. Validation is done with ad-hoc `if (!field)` checks. Fix: add Zod schemas per endpoint, ideally in a shared `src/modules/accounting/schemas/` directory.

- **Only one E2E test file** (`tests/e2e/navigation.spec.ts`) — No unit tests, no integration tests for any service. Fix: add unit tests for the pure utility functions (`formatCurrency`, `aging.ts`, `doubleEntry.ts`, `autoMatch.ts`) and service-layer integration tests for the most critical paths (journal entries, bank reconciliation, customer payments).

---

### Score: 5/10

### Summary

The codebase has a well-conceived module boundary (`src/modules/accounting/`) with a proper service layer, optimised auth middleware, and consistent CSS variable theming — these are genuine strengths. However, pervasive copy-paste across 100+ pages (39 copies of `formatCurrency`, 14 copies of `StatusBadge`, identical fetch-state boilerplate everywhere), a flat and inconsistently named API directory of 120+ files, 17 silent empty catch blocks, and near-total absence of custom hooks or shared UI components mean the codebase will become increasingly expensive to maintain and debug as it scales.

  The project's stack preference is `bun` (per `bun.lock` present) but the deploy script uses `npm install --production` and `npm run build`.   With `retries: 0` and no `webServer` block, running `test:e2e` against a dead server silently fails or produces misleading errors. Fix: add a `webServer: { command: 'bun run dev', url: 'http://localhost:3101', reuseExistingServer: true }` block.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customer_payments (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  payment_number VARCHAR(30),
  client_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id),
  payment_date DATE NOT NULL,

  bank_account_id UUID REFERENCES gl_accounts(id),
  description TEXT,
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN (
    'draft', 'confirmed', 'reconciled', 'cancelled'
  )),
  gl_journal_entry_id UUID REFERENCES gl_journal_entries(id),
  project_id UUID,
  created_by UUID NOT NULL,
  confirmed_by UUID,
  confirmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_cp_client ON customer_payments(client_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_cp_status ON customer_payments(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_cp_date ON customer_payments(payment_date);
CREATE INDEX idx_cp_project ON customer_payments(project_id) WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL;

-- ── Customer Payment Allocations ──────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customer_payment_allocations (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  payment_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES customer_payments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  invoice_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES customer_invoices(id),
  amount_allocated NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount_allocated > 0),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(payment_id, invoice_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_cpa_invoice ON customer_payment_allocations(invoice_id);

-- ── Credit Notes (Customer & Supplier) ────────────────────────────────────────

  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  credit_note_number VARCHAR(30),
  type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('customer', 'supplier')),
  -- Customer credit note refs
  client_id UUID REFERENCES customers(id),
  customer_invoice_id UUID REFERENCES customer_invoices(id),

  supplier_id UUID REFERENCES suppliers(id),

  credit_date DATE NOT NULL,
  reason TEXT,
  subtotal NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

  tax_amount NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,

  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'approved', 'applied', 'cancelled')),
  gl_journal_entry_id UUID REFERENCES gl_journal_entries(id),
  project_id UUID,
  created_by UUID NOT NULL,
  approved_by UUID,
  approved_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

## Dependencies & Infrastructure Analysis

### Critical Issues

**[package.json:38] `sonner` is installed but never imported anywhere in the codebase.**
The app uses `react-hot-toast` exclusively (15 import sites across pages and components). `sonner` at 2.0.7 is dead weight (~28KB gzipped) with zero usage. Additionally, there is no `<Toaster />` provider mounted in `pages/_app.tsx` — toasts are called but no provider renders them, meaning all toasts silently fail in production.
Fix: Remove `sonner`. Add `<Toaster />` from `react-hot-toast` to `pages/_app.tsx`.

**[package.json:32] `pg` is installed but never imported in application code.**
`pg` appears only in `scripts/run-migrations.mjs` (a dev/migration script). The application exclusively uses `@neondatabase/serverless` via `src/lib/neon.ts`. `pg` is a Node.js-only driver (~3MB) incompatible with edge runtimes and unnecessary at runtime.
Fix: Move `pg` to `devDependencies` (it's only needed for migrations). Or better: rewrite migrations to use `@neondatabase/serverless` and remove `pg` entirely.

**[package.json:17] `@types/formidable` is in `dependencies`, not `devDependencies`.**
Type packages are compile-time only and should never ship to production. This inflates the production `node_modules`.
Fix: Move to `devDependencies`.

**[scripts/deploy.sh:33] Deploy script uses `npm` despite the project having `bun.lock`.**
The repo has both `bun.lock` and `package-lock.json`, signalling lockfile split. The deploy script runs `npm install --production` which ignores `bun.lock`, can resolve different versions, and is significantly slower.
Fix: Standardise on one package manager. Since `bun` is in the stack preferences and a `bun.lock` exists, deploy should use `bun install --production`. Remove `package-lock.json`.

---

### Warnings

**[package.json:43] `xlsx` (v0.18.5) is installed but never statically imported.**
The only xlsx-related code is a file input `accept=".xlsx"` in `AccountingDocumentPanel.tsx` (which is just an HTML attribute). No `import XLSX` or `from 'xlsx'` exists anywhere in source. `xlsx` is ~750KB minified and has a [known security advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6).
Fix: Verify if xlsx export is planned. If not, remove it. If export is needed, load it dynamically (`await import('xlsx')`) so it doesn't hit the initial bundle.

**[package.json:37] `recharts` (v3.6.0) is installed but not imported in any `.tsx`/`.ts` source file.**
No `from 'recharts'` exists in `pages/` or `src/`. It's a large library (~500KB). `EnhancedStatCard.tsx` exists in the dashboard components but imports only from `lucide-react`.
Fix: Remove unless charting is planned; add dynamically if/when needed.

**[package.json:41] `jszip` is only used via dynamic import in one file.**
`pages/accounting/statement-run/index.tsx` uses `await import('jszip')` at runtime for bundling PDF statements into a ZIP. This is fine as a pattern (lazy-loaded), but `jszip` should remain as a dependency since it's genuinely used.
Fix: No change needed, but confirm the feature is active.

**[src/lib/neon.ts:103–120] The `transaction()` helper is broken for `@neondatabase/serverless` HTTP mode.**
The neon serverless HTTP client is stateless — each tagged template call is an independent HTTP request. Issuing `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` as separate calls does NOT guarantee they run on the same connection. For real transactions with the neon serverless driver, you must use `neon()` with `{ fullResults: true }` and the `transaction()` helper from `@neondatabase/serverless`, or use a `Pool` from `pg`.
Fix: Replace custom transaction wrapper with the official neon transaction API: `import { neon } from '@neondatabase/serverless'; const sql = neon(url); await sql.transaction([...queries])`.

**[package.json:28] `lucide-react` is pinned at `^0.279.0` (released ~mid-2023), now at v0.500+.**
Over 200 new icons and tree-shaking improvements have been added. The app uses lucide-react in 120+ files.
Fix: Upgrade to latest: `bun add lucide-react@latest`. Review any renamed icons (check changelog for breaking renames).

**[package.json:46–63] No unit testing library — only Playwright e2e.**
No Jest, Vitest, or similar is present. Business logic like `bankPdfParser.ts`, `reconReportPdf.ts`, and all accounting calculations have zero unit test coverage.
Fix: Add `vitest` to devDependencies and write unit tests for pure utility functions.

---

### Suggestions

**[package.json:22] `jspdf` + `jspdf-autotable` — legitimately used, but only in one utility.**
`src/modules/accounting/utils/reconReportPdf.ts` is the sole consumer. Both packages are static imports, meaning they land in the server bundle.
Fix: These are server-side only (PDF generation in API routes), so the impact is acceptable. Confirm they're not accidentally imported client-side.

**[package.json:30] `pdf-parse` — used only in `bankPdfParser.ts` via `require()` at runtime.**
The module uses `require('pdf-parse')` dynamically (lazy). This is correct for a server-side-only module.
Fix: No action needed, but add `// WORKING:` marker per code conventions.

**[scripts/nginx-app-isaflow:3] Nginx uses `Cloudflare Flexible SSL`.**
Flexible SSL means traffic between Cloudflare and your origin server is plain HTTP. If the origin server were ever exposed directly (misconfigured Cloudflare, IP leak), credentials and session tokens transit unencrypted.
Fix: Upgrade to Cloudflare `Full (strict)` SSL mode and provision a cert on the origin (e.g., via Let's Encrypt or Cloudflare Origin Certificate).

**[scripts/isaflow.service:1] No `MemoryLimit` or `CPUQuota` in the systemd unit.**
Next.js production can consume significant memory (confirmed by `--max-old-space-size=4096` in the build script). Without resource limits, a memory leak could take down the host.
Fix: Add `MemoryMax=1G` and `CPUQuota=80%` to the `[Service]` section.

**[scripts/isaflow.service:10] Node binary path is hardcoded to `/usr/bin/node`.**
If the server uses nvm or upgrades Node, the path can break silently.
Fix: Use `ExecStart=/usr/bin/env node /home/velo/isaflow/node_modules/.bin/next start -p 3101` or use `Type=forking` with a shell wrapper.

**[package.json:5-11] No `format` or `pre-commit` script.**
No Prettier, no Husky, no lint-staged. Code style enforcement is entirely optional.
Fix: Add `prettier` + `lint-staged` + Husky pre-commit hook.

**[package.json:29] `date-fns` v2 (not v3).**
date-fns v3 was released in late 2023 with ESM-first exports and smaller bundle. The package is not imported in any page or src file (0 matches found), making it a candidate for removal or it's used transitively.
Fix: Confirm if directly needed. If not, remove. If yes, upgrade to v3.

---

### Score: 4/10

**Summary:** The project has three immediately impactful bugs: toast notifications silently fail because no `<Toaster>` provider is mounted in `_app.tsx`, the `transaction()` helper in `neon.ts` is architecturally broken for a stateless HTTP client (BEGIN/COMMIT run on separate connections), and the deploy pipeline uses `npm` while the lockfile is `bun.lock`, creating reproducibility risk. On top of these, roughly 3 packages (`sonner`, `recharts`, `xlsx`) are installed and paid for in bundle size with zero actual usage, and `@types/formidable` shipping to production is a minor but unnecessary bloat.

`withRole` and `withPermission` middleware exist in `/src/lib/auth/middleware.ts` but are **never used** in any API route. After login, the app blindly calls `router.push(returnTo)` where `returnTo` comes directly from `router.query.returnTo`. An attacker can craft a link like `/login?returnTo=https://evil.com` and after a successful login the user is redirected to an external site.
**Fix:** Validate that `returnTo` is a relative path starting with `/`. Example: `const safeReturn = returnTo?.startsWith('/') ? returnTo : '/accounting'`.

**6. [`pages/api/auth/login.ts:112`, `pages/api/auth/logout.ts:38`] Cookie is not `SameSite: Strict`**
The auth cookie uses `sameSite: 'lax'`. For an accounting app with state-mutating POST endpoints, `'strict'` is more appropriate. `'lax'` still allows the cookie to be sent on top-level cross-site navigations (e.g., clicking a link from an email).
**Fix:** Change to `sameSite: 'strict'` on the `Set-Cookie` call in both login and logout. This also removes CSRF risk for the login endpoint itself.

**7. [`pages/api/accounting/` — 23 files] Direct `neon(process.env.DATABASE_URL!)` instantiation bypasses the central retry/resilience layer**
23 API route files create their own `neon()` instance with `process.env.DATABASE_URL!` (non-null assertion) instead of importing the shared `sql` from `@/lib/neon`. This bypasses the retry logic, WebSocket configuration, and health-check improvements in the central client. It also crashes the process at import time if `DATABASE_URL` is absent, instead of throwing a clean error.
**Fix:** Remove all local `const sql = neon(process.env.DATABASE_URL!)` declarations and import `import { sql } from '@/lib/neon'` uniformly. Affected files include `item-adjustments.ts`, `item-pricing.ts`, `documents.ts`, `customer-allocations.ts`, `supplier-allocations.ts`, and all files under `reports/`.

**8. [`src/lib/api-error-handler.ts:97`] Internal error messages leaked in production**
The `withErrorHandler` wrapper at line 97 sends `error.message` directly to the client as the response body: `const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : ...`. Database error messages (table names, column names, constraint names) can be exposed to clients even in production, aiding reconnaissance.
**Fix:** In `withErrorHandler`, replace line 97–103 with a generic message in production: `const errorMessage = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? 'An unexpected error occurred' : error.message`. Note that `apiResponse.internalError()` and `apiResponse.databaseError()` in `apiResponse.ts` handle this correctly — `withErrorHandler` has a separate, unguarded code path.

Bank statement imports accept base64 PDF content in the JSON body. The 2MB client-side check in `bank-tx-attachments.ts` is correct, but Next.js's default body parser accepts up to 1MB. Files larger than 1MB will be silently truncated or rejected by Next.js before the handler runs, while also not having an explicit `export const config = { api: { sizeLimit: '...' }}` to increase or confirm the limit.
**Fix:** Add `export const config = { api: { bodyParser: { sizeLimit: '3mb' } } }` to `bank-transactions-import.ts` and `bank-tx-attachments.ts`. Validate the decoded byte size server-side before processing.

**10. [No middleware file at `pages/_middleware.ts` or `middleware.ts`] No Next.js edge middleware — page routes are unguarded at the routing layer**
Auth is enforced only inside API handlers. Frontend pages under `/pages/accounting/*` have no server-side redirect guard. A user who clears their cookie can still GET the HTML of any accounting page (SSR data would be absent, but the page shells are publicly served).
**Fix:** Add a `middleware.ts` at the project root that reads the `ff_auth_token` cookie and redirects unauthenticated requests for `/accounting/*` to `/login?returnTo=<path>`.

**11. [`src/lib/auth/jwt.ts:19`] Access token lifetime is 24 hours — too long for a financial app**
A compromised token is valid for 24 hours. Standard practice for sensitive applications is 15–60 minutes with silent refresh.
**Fix:** Reduce `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY` to `'15m'` or `'1h'` and implement a token refresh mechanism using the existing 30-day session in the DB.

**12. [`next.config.js`] No HTTP security headers configured**
The `next.config.js` has no `headers()` function. This means no `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, or `Permissions-Policy` headers are set.
**Fix:** Add a `headers()` export to `next.config.js` with at minimum:
```js
'X-Frame-Options': 'DENY',
'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff',
'Referrer-Policy': 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin',
'Content-Security-Policy': "default-src 'self'; ..."
```

**13. [`pages/api/accounting/` — all routes] Input validation uses manual type assertions, not Zod**
`zod` is listed as a dependency in `package.json` but is not used in any API route. Inputs are typed via TypeScript `as` casts (e.g., `req.body as { email?: string }`) which provide no runtime validation. Invalid types passed in JSON bodies reach the database.
**Fix:** Define Zod schemas for API bodies and use `schema.safeParse(req.body)` at the top of each handler. Especially important for financial mutations like invoice creation, journal entries, and payment processing.

**14. [`pages/api/auth/login.ts:87-89`] `x-forwarded-for` header is taken at face value**
The IP address logged and stored in `user_sessions` is taken directly from `x-forwarded-for` without validation. A client can spoof this header arbitrarily (e.g., `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1`), making IP-based audit logs unreliable.
**Fix:** Only trust `x-forwarded-for` if you control the proxy. Use the rightmost untrusted IP, or configure the trusted proxy count explicitly. At minimum, sanitize/limit the value's length.

**15. [`src/lib/auth/jwt.ts:77-91`] `decodeToken()` function decodes without verification**
A public `decodeToken` utility exists that decodes a JWT without signature verification. It is marked as "for debugging" but is exported. If any route accidentally calls `decodeToken` instead of `verifyToken`, it silently accepts unsigned/forged tokens.
**Fix:** Make this function `private` (unexported) or remove it from the auth module's public API. Mark it clearly with a `// UNTESTED:` or `// DANGEROUS:` comment.

---

### Score: 5/10

**Summary:** The authentication foundation is solid — bcrypt at cost 12, HttpOnly cookies, session revocation via DB, and consistent `withAuth` coverage across all 130+ API routes are all production-quality choices. However, a weak/default JWT secret and live DB credentials in `.env.local` are immediate critical risks, and the complete absence of role-based enforcement means every authenticated user can perform year-end closings, run depreciation, and execute data migrations — unacceptable in a multi-user accounting system.

Build a SARS eFiling Integration module for the IsaFlow accounting app at /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting.

## Codebase Patterns (MUST follow exactly)
- Database: `import { sql } from '@/lib/neon'` — tagged templates
- API routes: `import { apiResponse } from '@/lib/apiResponse'` + `withAuth(withErrorHandler(handler as any))`  
- Pages use `AppLayout` from `@/components/layout/AppLayout`
- Colors: teal (#14b8a6) for accents
- Read existing files to understand patterns before writing

## What to Build

### 1. SARS Service (`src/modules/accounting/services/sarsService.ts`)

**VAT201 Generation:**
- `generateVAT201(periodStart: string, periodEnd: string)` — returns a structured VAT201 object:
  - Field 1: Total standard-rated supplies (15%)
  - Field 2: Total zero-rated supplies
  - Field 3: Total exempt supplies
  - Field 4: Total imports (zero if n/a)
  - Field 5: Total output VAT (Field1 × 15%)
  - Field 6-9: Input VAT categories
  - Field 10: Total input VAT
  - Field 11: VAT payable/refundable (output - input)
  - Pull data from customer_invoices (output) and supplier_invoices (input) for the period
  - Cross-reference with gl_accounts for VAT accounts

**EMP201 Generation (monthly PAYE/UIF/SDL):**
- `generateEMP201(periodStart: string, periodEnd: string)` — returns:
  - Total PAYE withheld
  - Total UIF (employee + employer)
  - Total SDL
  - Number of employees
  - Total taxable remuneration
  - Pull from payroll_runs and payslips tables (may not exist yet — handle gracefully with empty data)

**Tax Period Management:**
- `getTaxPeriods()` — list SA tax periods (bi-monthly VAT periods, monthly PAYE)
- `getComplianceCalendar()` — upcoming deadlines:
  - VAT201: Due by 25th of month following end of VAT period
  - EMP201: Due by 7th of month following payroll month
  - IRP5/IT3(a): Due with EMP501
  - EMP501: Due by end of May (interim) and end of October (annual)
  - Provisional Tax (IRP6): Due end of August and end of February

### 2. Database Migration (`scripts/migrations/sars-efiling.sql`)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sars_submissions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  form_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'VAT201', 'EMP201', 'EMP501', 'IRP5'
  period_start DATE NOT NULL,
  period_end DATE NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft', -- draft, generated, submitted, accepted, rejected
  form_data JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  submission_reference TEXT,
  submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  submitted_by UUID,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sars_compliance_events (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  event_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'VAT201_DUE', 'EMP201_DUE', 'EMP501_DUE', 'PROVISIONAL_TAX'
  due_date DATE NOT NULL,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending', -- pending, completed, overdue
  submission_id UUID REFERENCES sars_submissions(id),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

### 3. API Routes (`pages/api/accounting/sars/`)

**`sars-vat201.ts`**
- GET `?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD` — generate VAT201 data
- POST `{ periodStart, periodEnd }` — save as draft submission

**`sars-emp201.ts`**
- GET `?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD` — generate EMP201 data
- POST — save as draft

tool_input.content:
# AutoResearch Report: isaflow (Accounting App)

**Date:** 2026-03-27
**Files Analyzed:** ~6,713 TypeScript files
**Stack:** Next.js 14.2 (Pages Router), React 18, TypeScript (strict), Tailwind CSS, Neon Postgres, Zod (installed but unused)
**Issues Found:** 10 critical, 16 warnings, 18 suggestions

---

## Executive Summary

isaflow has a solid TypeScript-strict foundation with good auth primitives (bcrypt, HttpOnly cookies, session revocation) and a well-conceived module structure under `src/modules/accounting/`. However, the codebase suffers from **three systemic problems**: (1) pervasive copy-paste across 100+ pages with no shared utilities layer, (2) security gaps that are dangerous for a financial application (no RBAC enforcement, weak JWT secret, no rate limiting), and (3) missing DX infrastructure (no ESLint config, no Prettier, no CI, no unit tests). The app works but will become increasingly expensive to maintain and risky to operate as it scales.

---

## Overall Scores

| Dimension | Score | Status |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| Architecture | 5/10 | Needs shared utilities & hooks |
| Code Quality | 5.5/10 | `type Row = any` defeats strict TS |
| Performance | 4/10 | Fetch waterfalls, missing lazy loads |
| Security | 5/10 | Auth exists but RBAC not enforced |
| Developer Experience | 4.5/10 | No lint config, no CI, no tests |
| Dependencies | 4/10 | Dead deps, broken transactions |
| **Overall** | **4.7/10** | |

---

## Critical Issues (Fix Now)

### 1. SECURITY: JWT secret is a guessable default string
`.env.local:3` — `JWT_SECRET=accounting-app-jwt-secret-change-in-production`. Anyone who guesses this can forge tokens and log in as any user.
**Fix:** `openssl rand -base64 32` → set in production environment.

### 2. SECURITY: No role-based access control enforced on any endpoint
`withRole()` and `withPermission()` middleware exist but are **never called**. Any authenticated user can close fiscal years, run depreciation, execute Sage migrations, and perform year-end closings.
**Fix:** Wrap destructive endpoints with `withRole('admin')`: year-end, depreciation, sage-migration, fiscal-periods-action, opening-balances.

### 3. SECURITY: No rate limiting on login endpoint
`POST /api/auth/login` — unlimited password guesses with no lockout or CAPTCHA.
**Fix:** Add rate limiting (Upstash Redis or `next-rate-limit`), lock after N failures.

### 4. DEPS: `neon.ts` transaction helper is architecturally broken
`src/lib/neon.ts:103-120` — `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` issued as separate HTTP requests on the Neon serverless driver. Each runs on a different connection, so transactions don't actually work.
**Fix:** Use the official `sql.transaction([...queries])` API from `@neondatabase/serverless`.

### 5. DEPS: Toast notifications silently fail — no `<Toaster>` provider mounted
`react-hot-toast` is called in 15 files but no `<Toaster />` component is rendered in `_app.tsx`. All toast calls are no-ops.
**Fix:** Add `<Toaster />` to `pages/_app.tsx`. Remove unused `sonner` package.

### 6. QUALITY: `type Row = any` across all 29 service files
Every service file uses `type Row = any` for database results, defeating TypeScript strict mode at the entire data access layer.
**Fix:** Define typed row interfaces per query, or use `Record<string, unknown>` with assertion helpers.

### 7. QUALITY: Two parallel API response systems in active use
`src/lib/apiResponse.ts` and `src/lib/api-error-handler.ts` both define response helpers, used across 101 routes. Internal error messages leak to clients via the `withErrorHandler` path.
**Fix:** Consolidate to one system. Add production error masking.

### 8. ARCH: `formatCurrency` duplicated 39-43 times across pages
Every page defines its own identical `formatCurrency(amount)` with `en-ZA`/`ZAR` locale. Same for `formatDate` (9x) and `StatusBadge` (14x).
**Fix:** Create `src/utils/formatters.ts` and `src/components/ui/StatusBadge.tsx`.

### 9. PERF: 7-request serial waterfall on bank transactions page
`pages/accounting/bank-transactions/index.tsx:93-139` — Seven `fetch()` calls fire sequentially in a `useEffect`.
**Fix:** Wrap in `Promise.all([...])`.

### 10. DX: No ESLint config file exists — linting runs with zero rules
ESLint packages are installed but no `.eslintrc.*` exists. The lint script also only covers `src/`, missing all `pages/`.
**Fix:** Create `.eslintrc.json` with `@typescript-eslint/recommended` + React rules. Lint both `src/` and `pages/`.

---

## Warnings (Fix Soon)

### Security
11. **Open redirect** via unvalidated `returnTo` query param in `pages/login.tsx:22-23`. Fix: validate it starts with `/`.
12. **No Next.js middleware** — page routes serve HTML shells to unauthenticated users. Fix: add `middleware.ts` with auth redirect.
13. **23 API routes bypass central DB client** — create their own `neon()` instance, skipping retry logic. Fix: import `sql` from `@/lib/neon` uniformly.
14. **Internal error messages leak** in `withErrorHandler` production responses. Fix: mask in production.
15. **`x-forwarded-for` taken at face value** — IP audit logs can be spoofed. Fix: trust only from known proxy.

### Architecture & Quality
16. **9 silent empty catch blocks** in bank-transactions page alone (17 total across app). Fix: at minimum log errors.
17. **Zero Zod validation on any API route** despite Zod being installed. All inputs are `as`-cast. Fix: add schemas.
18. **Inconsistent API route naming** — 120+ flat files with mixed `noun-verb.ts` vs `noun.ts` patterns. Fix: adopt resource directories.
19. **Inconsistent page routing** — 15 flat `.tsx` pages vs 85+ directory-pattern pages. Fix: standardize.
20. **bankReconciliationService.ts is 1,153 lines**, bank-transactions/index.tsx is 958 lines. Fix: split.
21. **`@ts-expect-error` for auth middleware** in 4 API routes. Fix: use `AuthenticatedNextApiRequest` type.

### Performance
22. **Static jsPDF import** in `reconReportPdf.ts` (~500KB). Fix: dynamic import (pattern exists in `statementPdf.ts`).
23. **Google Fonts `<link>`** in `_document.tsx` is render-blocking. Fix: use `next/font/google`.

tool_input.prompt:
Build a Document OCR / Receipt Capture module for the IsaFlow accounting app at /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting.

## Codebase Patterns (MUST follow exactly)
- Database: `import { sql } from '@/lib/neon'` — tagged templates
- API routes: `import { apiResponse } from '@/lib/apiResponse'` + `withAuth(withErrorHandler(handler as any))`
- Pages use `AppLayout` from `@/components/layout/AppLayout`
- File uploads use `formidable` (already installed v3.5.4) — see existing bank statement import for pattern
- Colors: teal (#14b8a6) for accents
- Read existing files first to understand patterns

## What to Build

### 1. OCR Service (`src/modules/accounting/services/ocrService.ts`)

**Receipt/Invoice Text Extraction:**
Since we can't rely on external OCR APIs being available, build a pattern-based extraction engine that works with text-based PDFs (using pdf-parse, already installed) and provides a manual-entry fallback for images.

- `extractFromPdf(buffer: Buffer): Promise<ExtractedDocument>` — parse PDF text and extract:
  - Vendor name (look for company names at top of document)
  - Date (look for date patterns: DD/MM/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD, etc.)
  - Total amount (look for "Total", "Amount Due", "Balance Due" followed by currency)
  - VAT amount (look for "VAT", "Tax" near amounts)
  - Invoice/reference number (look for "Invoice", "Ref", "INV-" patterns)
  - Line items if possible

- `extractFromText(rawText: string): Promise<ExtractedDocument>` — same extraction from raw text

Pattern matchers for SA documents:
- Currency: R, ZAR, R followed by number
- VAT: 15% standard, look for "VAT Reg" for vendor VAT number
- Date formats: DD/MM/YYYY, DD-MM-YYYY, DD Month YYYY
- Common invoice headers: "TAX INVOICE", "CREDIT NOTE", "STATEMENT"

### 2. Types
```typescript
interface ExtractedDocument {
  documentType: 'invoice' | 'credit_note' | 'receipt' | 'statement' | 'unknown';
  vendorName: string | null;
  vendorVatNumber: string | null;
  date: string | null;           // YYYY-MM-DD
  referenceNumber: string | null;
  subtotal: number | null;
  vatAmount: number | null;
  totalAmount: number | null;
  lineItems: ExtractedLineItem[];
  rawText: string;
  confidence: number;            // 0-1
  warnings: string[];
}

interface ExtractedLineItem {
  description: string;
  quantity: number | null;
  unitPrice: number | null;
  total: number | null;
}
```

### 3. Database Migration (`scripts/migrations/document-capture.sql`)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS captured_documents (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  file_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  file_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'pdf', 'image'
  file_size INTEGER,
  document_type TEXT, -- 'invoice', 'credit_note', 'receipt', 'statement'
  extracted_data JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
  vendor_name TEXT,
  document_date DATE,
  reference_number TEXT,
  total_amount NUMERIC(15,2),
  vat_amount NUMERIC(15,2),
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending', -- pending, reviewed, matched, rejected
  matched_invoice_id UUID,
  matched_bank_tx_id UUID,
  notes TEXT,
  uploaded_by UUID,
```

-- Approval Workflows
-- Configurable approval rules for invoices, payments, journal entries, credit notes

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS approval_rules (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  document_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'customer_invoice', 'supplier_invoice', 'payment', 'journal_entry', 'credit_note'
  condition_field TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'total', -- 'total', 'amount'
  condition_operator TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'greater_than', -- 'greater_than', 'greater_equal', 'any'
  condition_value NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  approver_role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'admin', -- 'admin', 'manager', 'accountant'
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  priority INTEGER DEFAULT 100,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS approval_requests (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  rule_id UUID REFERENCES approval_rules(id),
  document_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  document_id UUID NOT NULL,
  document_reference TEXT, -- INV-001, JE-042, etc.
  amount NUMERIC(15,2),
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', -- pending, approved, rejected, cancelled
  requested_by UUID NOT NULL,
  requested_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  decided_by UUID,
  decided_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  decision_notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

SUMMARY: Built complete Invoice PDF generation and Email delivery system for IsaFlow accounting app.

## Files Created

### Services
- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/src/modules/accounting/services/invoicePdfService.ts`** -- `generateInvoicePdf(invoiceId)` and `generateCreditNotePdf(creditNoteId)` functions. Queries invoice + line items + client details from DB, generates professional A4 PDF using jsPDF + jspdf-autotable with teal (#14b8a6) header bar, company/client sections, line items table, totals with VAT, payment details (bank info), terms, and page footers. Returns `Buffer`.

- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/src/modules/accounting/services/emailService.ts`** -- Generic `sendEmail(options)` using nodemailer with SMTP config from env vars (SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, SMTP_FROM). Gracefully returns `{ success: false }` if SMTP not configured. Also includes `sendInvoiceEmail(invoiceId, recipientEmail)` which generates the PDF, sends it as attachment with a professional HTML email template (table-based, inline CSS for email client compatibility), and updates tracking columns on the invoice.

### API Routes
- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/pages/api/accounting/invoice-pdf.ts`** -- GET `?invoiceId=UUID` returns PDF download
- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/pages/api/accounting/invoice-email.ts`** -- POST `{ invoiceId, recipientEmail }` generates + sends + tracks
- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/pages/api/accounting/credit-note-pdf.ts`** -- GET `?creditNoteId=UUID` returns credit note PDF download

### Migration
- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/scripts/migrations/invoice-emails.sql`** -- Adds `email_sent_at`, `email_sent_to`, `email_message_id` columns to `customer_invoices`

## Files Modified

- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/pages/accounting/customer-invoices/[invoiceId].tsx`** -- Added "Download PDF" button (opens in new tab) and "Email Invoice" button (opens modal with pre-filled recipient email from client record, sends via API, shows success/error feedback, displays last-sent info)

- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/pages/accounting/credit-notes/[creditNoteId].tsx`** -- Added "Download PDF" button

- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/pages/api/accounting/customer-invoices-detail.ts`** -- Added `client_email` to the SELECT query so invoice detail API returns it for email pre-fill

- **`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/package.json`** -- Added `nodemailer` and `@types/nodemailer` dependencies

All new code follows existing patterns: `withAuth(withErrorHandler(handler as any))` for API routes, `sql` tagged templates for DB queries, `apiResponse` helpers, `log` instead of console, dynamic jsPDF imports. TypeScript compiles clean (no new errors).

SUMMARY:

Built a complete KPI Dashboard for the IsaFlow accounting app across three files:

**1. KPI Service** (`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/src/modules/accounting/services/kpiService.ts`)
- `getDashboardKPIs()` - Revenue, expenses, gross/net profit, cash position, AR/AP totals with overdue amounts, debtor/creditor days, activity counts. Includes prior period comparison for % change.
- `getRevenueChart()` - Monthly revenue vs expenses using `generate_series` for N months
- `getCashFlowChart()` - Monthly bank transaction inflows vs outflows
- `getAgingBreakdown('ar'|'ap')` - Current/30/60/90+ day buckets
- `getTopCustomers()` - Top N customers by invoice revenue
- `getTopExpenseCategories()` - Top N GL expense accounts by total

All queries use `import { sql } from '@/lib/neon'` tagged templates, matching existing service patterns.

**2. API Route** (`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/pages/api/accounting/kpi-dashboard.ts`)
- GET endpoint with `from`, `to`, `months` query params (defaults: current month start, today, 6 months)
- Uses `apiResponse` + `withAuth(withErrorHandler(handler as any))` pattern
- Runs all 7 service calls in parallel via `Promise.all`

**3. Dashboard Page** (`/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting/pages/accounting/index.tsx`)
- Replaced the `OverviewTab` component content with the KPI dashboard
- Row 1: 4 metric cards (Revenue with % change, Gross Profit with margin, Cash Position, Outstanding AR with overdue)

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy IsaFlow App to Velocity Server
set -e

DEPLOY_DIR="/home/velo/isaflow"
REPO_DIR="/home/hein/Workspace/Accounting"
SERVICE_NAME="isaflow"

echo "=== Deploying IsaFlow ==="

# 1. Sync files to deploy directory
echo "Syncing files..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "
  mkdir -p $DEPLOY_DIR
  rsync -a --delete \
    --exclude=node_modules \
    --exclude=.next \
    --exclude=.git \
    --exclude=.env.local \
    --exclude=tests \
    --exclude=test-results \
    $REPO_DIR/ $DEPLOY_DIR/
"

# 2. Copy env file if not exists
if [ ! -f "$DEPLOY_DIR/.env.local" ]; then
  echo "Creating .env.local..."
  sudo -u velo bash -c "cp $REPO_DIR/.env.local $DEPLOY_DIR/.env.local"
fi

# 3. Install deps and build
echo "Installing dependencies..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "cd $DEPLOY_DIR && npm install --production"

echo "Building..."
sudo -u velo bash -c "cd $DEPLOY_DIR && npm run build"

# 4. Install systemd service
if [ ! -f /etc/systemd/system/${SERVICE_NAME}.service ]; then
  echo "Installing systemd service..."
  sudo cp $REPO_DIR/scripts/${SERVICE_NAME}.service /etc/systemd/system/
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo systemctl enable $SERVICE_NAME
fi

# 5. Install nginx config if not exists
if [ ! -f /etc/nginx/sites-available/app-isaflow ]; then
  echo "Installing nginx config..."
  sudo cp $REPO_DIR/scripts/nginx-app-isaflow /etc/nginx/sites-available/app-isaflow
  sudo ln -sf /etc/nginx/sites-available/app-isaflow /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/app-isaflow
  sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
fi

# 6. Restart service
echo "Restarting service..."
sudo systemctl restart $SERVICE_NAME

# 7. Check status
sleep 2
sudo systemctl status $SERVICE_NAME --no-pager | head -15

echo ""
echo "=== Deploy complete ==="
echo "App: https://app.isaflow.co.za"

tool_input.prompt:
In /home/hein/Workspace/Accounting, there are many page files with empty catch blocks like `.catch(() => {})` that silently swallow errors.

Your task:
1. Use Grep to find all files under `pages/` with the pattern `.catch(() => {})` or `.catch(() => { })` or `catch {}` or `catch (e) {}`
2. For each occurrence in page files (NOT in API routes — those have proper error handling), replace empty catches with:
   - For fetch chains: `.catch((err) => { log.warn('Failed to load [description]', { error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) }, '[PageName]'); })`
   - But actually, these pages don't import the logger. So instead, use a simpler pattern: `.catch(() => { /* non-critical: [description] */ })` — add a comment explaining WHAT failed so it's not truly silent.

Actually, the better approach for these fetch `.catch(() => {})` calls is: since these are client-side fetches loading reference data (bank accounts, GL accounts, etc.), a truly empty catch is acceptable IF the page already has error state handling. But the problem flagged was specifically about the bank-transactions page having 9 of them.

For the bank-transactions page (`pages/accounting/bank-transactions/index.tsx`), the fetches at lines 94-141 all have `.catch(() => {})`. These should at minimum have a descriptive comment. Update them to:
`.catch(() => { /* reference data load failure — non-critical, UI gracefully handles empty lists */ })`

For other pages with the same pattern, add similar descriptive comments to the catch blocks.

Focus on files with 3+ empty catch blocks. Use Grep to find them, then fix each one.
